subject: duck
review_scope: Independent visual comparison of source-keys.png, design.png, revisions/keys-v1.png and source.json only. Four chronological still keys in 2x2 order; no normal-speed playback inspected and no motion approval.

timed_key_evidence.evidence: Source duck has a left-facing bill over a forward-facing, planted body. Drawing preserves the leftward head/bill and two broad grounded feet.
Source faces forward with the bill directed down the image, while body and feet stay planted. Drawing supplies a frontal head, two visible eyes and a downward frontal bill over the same stance.

Source remains near frontal, with the bill pointing toward the viewer/downward. Drawing instead turns the head strongly to image right and presents a long lateral bill with one visible eye, adding a view change unsupported by this source key.
Source again has a near-frontal head and planted feet. Drawing returns toward frontal/three-quarter view while retaining the same feet and body support.

main_gap: The 2.2-second key invents a strong right-facing head turn where the source remains near frontal. Body support and recognizably simple angular duck construction are otherwise coherent.
bounded_repair: Redraw only the head and bill in the 2.2-second key as the source’s near-frontal view, with both eye positions readable and a foreshortened downward bill; preserve the neck attachment, body, wings and planted feet.
protected_strengths: Feet and body remain planted across all four keys.
Both legs connect coherently into broad angular webbed feet.
The long neck, simple outline and angular bill/feet keep the selected QuickDraw duck identity recognizable.
The first two keys clearly distinguish left-facing from frontal head views.
